semantic_callouts.label: CORE IDEA
semantic_callouts.meaning: The invariant or distinction the reader should retain.
semantic_callouts.where_use: One short takeaway on a chapter opening, or the existing mechanism summary on a code-defense spread.
semantic_callouts.do_not_use_for: Do not make a green panel imply eligibility, consent or a passing gate.

semantic_callouts.label: TRACE IT
semantic_callouts.meaning: A concrete path to follow through a figure or source excerpt.
semantic_callouts.where_use: The diagram prompt and the continuous code excerpt. Keep its existing question or figure ID visible.
semantic_callouts.do_not_use_for: Do not introduce a new source path, a fictional sequence or an unimplemented integration.

semantic_callouts.label: PROBE
semantic_callouts.meaning: An active-recall task that changes one ordering, failure point or constraint.
semantic_callouts.where_use: Endnote recall prompt, existing counterfactual and answered follow-up probes.
semantic_callouts.do_not_use_for: Do not present a proposed alternative as implemented behavior or an original design motivation.

semantic_callouts.label: WATCH FOR
semantic_callouts.meaning: A tempting inference that the evidence does not support.
semantic_callouts.where_use: Existing watch_for text, known release limits and the trap in a challenge card.
semantic_callouts.do_not_use_for: Do not invent a risk or add a warning to every paragraph.

usage_notes: Use one repeated color family per chapter, with a narrow ribbon or rule and a pale study-rail tint. Keep long reading text near black on white.
Keep the same semantic callout label throughout the book. Color supports the printed label and layout; it never carries technical meaning by itself.
Opening reading order: concrete hook, finish line, three anchor IDs. Put the recall and diagram prompts together at the chapter end for retrieval practice.
Keep chapter cues outside the technical answers. Preserve the printed source references, question IDs, figure captions and all evidence limitations.
Use the darkest ink value for small colored text; reserve the brighter accent for rules and larger labels. Check contrast after the final print palette is applied.
Avoid full-page color backgrounds and heavy fills. Pale tints, line art and white note areas keep duplex pages readable and economical to print.
The cues reference the current F01–F19 numbering. Chapter 1 uses the authority figure in the shared opening material; chapter 15 uses its existing blocking-call case.
